domain.name: Logistics, Transportation & Dispatch
domain.description: Practical routing, dispatch, vehicle readiness, trip communication, pricing, incidents, records, and capacity planning.

competencies.name: Route Planning
competencies.description: Plan efficient routes around stops, time windows, travel time, service time, and constraints.
competencies.purpose: Plan efficient routes around stops, time windows, travel time, service time, and constraints.

units.title: Route Planning: core principle
units.content: The least flexible commitment should shape the rest of the route.

units.title: Route Planning: working procedure
units.content: List fixed-time stops; pickup/dropoff constraints; travel; parking/load time; fuel/tolls; driver limits; recovery buffer; sequence around hard constraints.

units.title: Route Planning: common failures
units.content: Avoid treating map travel time as total service time, no parking/loading buffer, and impossible back-to-back stops.

drills.title: Practice Route Planning
drills.prompt: Plan a multi-city weekend with pickups, hotel, dinner, event, late-night return, and next-day travel.

competencies.name: Dispatch & Scheduling
competencies.description: Assign vehicles, drivers, jobs, and timing while preserving capacity and recovery options.
competencies.purpose: Assign vehicles, drivers, jobs, and timing while preserving capacity and recovery options.

units.title: Dispatch & Scheduling: core principle
units.content: Tight utilization is not efficient if one delay cascades through the entire day.

units.title: Dispatch & Scheduling: working procedure
units.content: Track job, client, pickup, destination, window, vehicle, driver, passenger/load needs, status, and exceptions; resolve conflicts before confirmation.

units.title: Dispatch & Scheduling: common failures
units.content: Avoid vehicle double-booking, hidden handoffs, no turnaround time, unclear status ownership, and inconsistent change communication.

drills.title: Practice Dispatch & Scheduling
drills.prompt: Schedule overlapping airport, school, and event trips across two vehicles and identify conflicts.

competencies.name: Vehicle Readiness & Pre-Trip Checks
competencies.description: Confirm a vehicle is safe, fueled, equipped, and documented before service.
competencies.purpose: Confirm a vehicle is safe, fueled, equipped, and documented before service.

units.title: Vehicle Readiness & Pre-Trip Checks: core principle
units.content: Warning lights or new brake, steering, overheating, tire, or electrical symptoms should be escalated rather than normalized.

units.title: Vehicle Readiness & Pre-Trip Checks: working procedure
units.content: Check tires, lights, mirrors, alerts/fluids, fuel/charge, wipers, doors/seatbelts, cleanliness, documents, emergency kit, and known defects.

units.title: Vehicle Readiness & Pre-Trip Checks: common failures
units.content: Avoid departing with known critical defects, overload, expired documents, or no roadside contingency.

drills.title: Practice Vehicle Readiness & Pre-Trip Checks
drills.prompt: Create a paid-service pre-trip checklist for a 15-passenger van.

competencies.name: Trip & Client Communication
competencies.description: Keep clients and passengers informed about confirmation, pickup, delays, changes, and completion.
competencies.purpose: Keep clients and passengers informed about confirmation, pickup, delays, changes, and completion.

units.title: Trip & Client Communication: core principle
units.content: Communicate material changes before the client has to ask.

units.title: Trip & Client Communication: working procedure
units.content: Confirm itinerary/contact; send reminder; give pickup instructions; surface delays with revised ETA; confirm major changes; close with completion/payment follow-up.

units.title: Trip & Client Communication: common failures
units.content: Avoid vague pickup locations, multiple unofficial itineraries, silent delays, and major verbal-only changes.

drills.title: Practice Trip & Client Communication
drills.prompt: Structure a message for a 25-minute delay with revised ETA and recovery plan.

competencies.name: Transportation Costing & Pricing
competencies.description: Estimate trip cost using time, mileage, vehicle, driver, tolls, parking, deadhead, risk, and margin.
competencies.purpose: Estimate trip cost using time, mileage, vehicle, driver, tolls, parking, deadhead, risk, and margin.

units.title: Transportation Costing & Pricing: core principle
units.content: Waiting time still consumes driver and vehicle capacity even when mileage is low.

units.title: Transportation Costing & Pricing: working procedure
units.content: Estimate vehicle cost, fuel/energy, tolls/parking, labor including wait/deadhead, rental, contingency, overhead contribution, and target margin.

units.title: Transportation Costing & Pricing: common failures
units.content: Avoid excluding deadhead, undercounting late-night hours, treating deposits as extra revenue, or pricing only from competitors.

drills.title: Practice Transportation Costing & Pricing
drills.prompt: Build a cost framework for a three-day group trip with late-night service, tolls, rental van, and waiting.

competencies.name: Roadside Incident Handling
competencies.description: Respond to breakdowns, accidents, illness, severe delays, or route disruptions safely.
competencies.purpose: Respond to breakdowns, accidents, illness, severe delays, or route disruptions safely.

units.title: Roadside Incident Handling: core principle
units.content: Safety outranks schedule when an abnormal event occurs.

units.title: Roadside Incident Handling: working procedure
units.content: Secure immediate safety; call emergency/roadside support as appropriate; account for passengers; notify client/dispatcher; arrange recovery transport; document facts and receipts.

units.title: Roadside Incident Handling: common failures
units.content: Avoid unsafe roadside repairs, moving an unsafe vehicle only to avoid towing, arguing fault at the scene, and delayed notification.

drills.title: Practice Roadside Incident Handling
drills.prompt: Plan actions for a passenger van that loses charging power 90 minutes from destination.

competencies.name: Transportation Records & Compliance Awareness
competencies.description: Maintain trip, vehicle, payment, and regulatory records appropriate to the service.
competencies.purpose: Maintain trip, vehicle, payment, and regulatory records appropriate to the service.

units.title: Transportation Records & Compliance Awareness: core principle
units.content: Commercial/passenger obligations depend on jurisdiction and service type, so current requirements must be verified.

units.title: Transportation Records & Compliance Awareness: working procedure
units.content: Maintain trip logs, driver/vehicle assignment, inspections/defects, insurance/registration, contracts/quotes, payments, incidents, and maintenance history; flag legal/compliance questions for current verification.

units.title: Transportation Records & Compliance Awareness: common failures
units.content: Avoid assuming personal coverage applies to paid service, relying on expired documents, or treating general guidance as jurisdiction-specific law.

drills.title: Practice Transportation Records & Compliance Awareness
drills.prompt: Define records to retain for paid passenger transportation and identify which requirements need current jurisdiction verification.

competencies.name: Capacity & Passenger Experience
competencies.description: Match vehicle, luggage, accessibility, comfort, and service level to the trip.
competencies.purpose: Match vehicle, luggage, accessibility, comfort, and service level to the trip.

units.title: Capacity & Passenger Experience: core principle
units.content: Nominal seat count is not the same as usable capacity once luggage, comfort, exits, and special needs are considered.

units.title: Capacity & Passenger Experience: working procedure
units.content: Confirm passenger count, luggage/equipment, seating, accessibility, trip duration, climate, charging/power needs, and pickup environment before assignment.

units.title: Capacity & Passenger Experience: common failures
units.content: Avoid last-minute luggage surprises, blocked exits, unsecured cargo, insufficient climate control, and assuming every passenger can board identically.

drills.title: Practice Capacity & Passenger Experience
drills.prompt: Evaluate vehicle fit for 11 travelers with weekend luggage, formalwear, and multi-hour legs.
